title: Case C — 3 × 3 block array
summary: 3 x 3 array of 0.20 m cubes, centre block at 0D / 1D / 2D, pedestrian-height scalar speed (thermistor), 3 wind directions.

configuration.array: 3 x 3 cubes, D = 0.20 m, block centres at x, y in {-0.4, 0, +0.4} m (pitch 0.40 m = 2D, street width D)

centre_building.1D: 0.2 x 0.2 x 0.2 m (same as the surroundings)

configuration.configurations_note: 3 centre-building heights x 3 wind directions; all nine share the identical 120-point set
configuration.measurement_height_note: z = 0.1 D for every point (2.0 m at the 1:100 scale Eddy3D solves it at)
configuration.U_H_note: U at z = D = 0.20 m from AF_caseC.csv; the data paper states U_H = 3.65 m/s
configuration.instrument: thermistor anemometer (omnidirectional scalar speed), 1 Hz, 30 s per point; approach flow by I-type hot wire, 500 Hz, 30 s
configuration.tunnel: Technology Development Division, Fujita Corporation, Tokyo
configuration.pitch_note: The 0.40 m pitch is read from MP-z-caseC.png and Figure 3 of the data paper (street = D); the 120-point grid alone bounds the pitch to (0.35, 0.40] m (the 49 absent nodes of the 13 x 13 grid are exactly the nine footprints for 0.375 m as well as 0.40 m).

frame.origin: array centre on the ground plane (centre of the middle block)
frame.x: +x streamwise at WD = 0 (checked three ways on the data: y -> -y is a symmetry, the x <= -0.25 band is faster than x >= +0.25 in every configuration, and the regression slope of Vs is most negative within 0.8-4.3 deg of +x)
frame.wind_direction_rotation: In the CSV's own frame WD rotates the wind from +x TOWARD -y (the WD = 45 field is mirror-symmetric about y = -x to within the experiment's repeatability, 0.10-0.13 m/s, and not about y = +x, 0.5-0.8 m/s). Figure 3 of the data paper draws the fan rotating toward +y. The two disagree by a y-sign flip; this release keeps the CSV frame, which is the frame the point coordinates live in. The disagreement is invisible at WD = 0.

inflow_fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares on AF_caseC.csv (16 points, z = 0.01 ... 1.2 m); two windows, because Case C scores at ONE height (z = 0.02 m) and the near-ground half of the fit matters
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; the tunnel profile is closer to a power law than a log law, so a log-law inlet carries a ~2.3 % rms residual over the fitted range

fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares on AF_caseC.csv (16 points, z = 0.01 ... 1.2 m); two windows, because Case C scores at ONE height (z = 0.02 m) and the near-ground half of the fit matters
fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ; the tunnel profile is closer to a power law than a log law, so a log-law inlet carries a ~2.3 % rms residual over the fitted range

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): a log-law inlet fitted to the case's own approach-flow file, with k and epsilon from the standard neutral ABL relations. Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) = u*/kappa ln((z + z0)/z0); k = u*^2 / sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))
recommended.fit: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares on AF_caseC.csv (16 points, z = 0.01 ... 1.2 m); two windows, because Case C scores at ONE height (z = 0.02 m) and the near-ground half of the fit matters; the first window, [0.02, 0.4]
recommended.openfoam: atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity / atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon with Uref, Zref, z0 and d = 0; nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 on the ground: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds them

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: U_H = U(z = D = 0.20 m) of the approach flow

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (requirements.txt)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: The measured quantity Vs is the MEAN OMNIDIRECTIONAL SCALAR speed from a thermistor, not |mean velocity vector|. A RANS |U| is biased low against it; the data paper suggests comparing sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) as a conservative correction (over all 1080 rows no Vs is below 0.13 U_H).
The 'CB' column is TEXT ('0D', '1D', '2D'); a reader that parses every field as a number gets NaN for it. The header ends with a trailing comma (an empty 8th column).

1080 rows = 3 wind directions x 3 centre buildings x 120 points, not 3 configurations. In the 0D configuration the 25 centre grid nodes are still absent although the ground there is free: the grid is held constant across configurations.
24 of the 120 points sit exactly on a building face plane (|x| = 0.30 or |y| = 0.30) in the open gap between two blocks: legitimate fluid points, but a probe's cell lookup is delicate there.
Point numbers 1, 2, 3, 34, 35, 36, 37, 46, 55, 100, 101, 102 do not occur (No. runs 4 ... 132 with nine interior gaps).
Experimental repeatability, from the mirror-symmetric point pairs: mean |dVs| 0.088-0.137 m/s (0.024-0.038 U_H).
